record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the cooperative and noncooperative characterizations obtained by de Clippel and Minelli for bargaining with verifiable types be extended to the harder setting in which players' types remain unverifiable even at the stage where the mechanism is used to make decisions?

evidence.quote: An obvious open problem is the extension of these results when types remain unverifiable, even at the decision stage.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-person bargaining problem with incomplete information in which each player i ∈ {1,2} privately observes a type t_i drawn from a finite set T_i according to a commonly known prior. A (direct) mechanism is a mapping that, given a profile of reported types, selects a (possibly random) decision/outcome from a feasible set X, yielding interim expected utilities U_i(t_i) for each player and each type.

In the verifiable-types setting, types reported at the implementation (decision) stage can be checked, so deviations in reporting can be punished or ruled out; in this setting, both a cooperative axiomatic characterization and a noncooperative bargaining-game characterization of a distinguished interim bargaining solution have been established. The cooperative characterization axiomatizes the solution on the interim utility frontier (using axioms such as efficiency, individual rationality, scale invariance, and a suitable independence/contraction property adapted to incomplete information), while the noncooperative characterization shows that the solution arises as the (limit of) equilibrium outcomes of an explicit alternating-offers or principal-style bargaining procedure.

Problem. Extend both the cooperative (axiomatic) characterization and the noncooperative (strategic) characterization of this two-person interim bargaining solution to the harder setting in which players' types remain unverifiable even at the stage at which the mechanism is actually used to make decisions, so that incentive-compatibility constraints must hold at the implementation stage and no type-contingent verification is available. Specifically: identify a solution concept on the set of interim-incentive-compatible, interim-individually-rational mechanisms, give a system of axioms that uniquely characterizes it, and exhibit a noncooperative bargaining game whose equilibria implement it.
artifact.category_tag: Cooperative game theory with incomplete information
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by de Clippel, Fanning, and Rozen ("Bargaining over Contingent Contracts Under Incomplete Information," AER 2022) and related work by Miyagawa and by Okada has addressed bargaining under incomplete information without verifiability, but it is not clear from available sources that this exactly extends both the cooperative and noncooperative characterizations of de Clippel–Minelli to the fully unverifiable decision-stage setting. Status appears unresolved in the precise form posed.

status_evidence.title: Bargaining over Contingent Contracts Under Incomplete Information
status_evidence.snippet: De Clippel, Fanning, and Rozen study bargaining under incomplete information with contingent contracts, extending earlier work.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends the bargaining framework, but does not fully replicate both characterizations in the unverifiable decision-stage setting.

status_evidence.title: Two-person bargaining with verifiable information
status_evidence.snippet: De Clippel and Minelli provide cooperative and noncooperative characterizations under verifiable types.
status_evidence.claim: Original characterizations are explicitly restricted to verifiable types.

status_evidence.title: Noncooperative Foundation of Nash Bargaining Solution under Incomplete Information (Miyagawa)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies noncooperative foundations of bargaining solutions under incomplete information.
status_evidence.claim: Related strategic foundations exist but do not form a definitive joint extension.
